correctness.rationale: With L_Kn=nI−11^T, PSD of diag(d_i)−11^T is equivalent to d_i>0 and Σ1/d_i≤1. The strict tangent inequality for 1/x gives a global unique least-cost prescribed-rate allocation, with active d_i proportional to 1/sqrt(p_i) and inactive d_i=n−λ. Solving the reciprocal equality yields exactly ell_q=q−T_q/sqrt(p_(q+1)), 1<=q<n, ordered thresholds, and F=(n−λ)(T_q²/(q−λ)−P_q); final all-active F=T_n²+(λ−n)P_n. At adjacent entry boundaries first derivatives P_q+(n−q)p_(q+1) agree, inverse rate is C1 concave and finally affine. n=3 prices(1,4,9) exact eigenspectra for budgets 8 and 10 match the stated unique gains and optimum; separately constrained numerical checks confirm those finite examples.
